contract.interface:
The target is strongly polynomial arbitrary rational LP: poly(m,n) arithmetic operations/comparisons independent of coefficient magnitudes, with polynomial intermediate rational encoding length. The campaign obtains restricted block operations and scoped obstructions, not a general LP algorithm or an impossibility theorem. Completion NOT_ACHIEVED; external correctness and priority UNKNOWN.

For explicitly acquired one-negative-resource feedback bundles, exact Schur/M-matrix elimination either closes all protected coordinates in O(k^3+nk) rational operations or supplies an improving recession certificate. This resums an Omega(2^L) local-batching example without a spectral-gap search. Classical M-matrix/Leontief principles are credited. Selecting the bundle and bounding the number of changed bundles remain unpaid.

General signed resources obey x-Qu with u>=0. An acquired inverse-positive Q or nonnegative right inverse closes the protected stocks; additional guard rows must be checked and can truncate the move. Exact counterexamples show admissible full blocks without admissible two-by-two subblocks, and a rectangular right inverse without any monotone square basis. Given full row rank and an acquired v>0 with Qv=0, add suitable multiples of v to an algebraic right inverse to make it nonnegative in strongly polynomial arithmetic, with polynomial bit lengths. Checking Q1=0 can supply v=1 cheaply.

Optimizing profit among such closures still contains arbitrary feasible bounded rational LP, even with Q1=0 and this repair available. The acquisition-preserving reduction charges denominator clearing, determinant bounds and encoding lengths. Appending the objective as another protected resource breaks the repair: a strictly positive cost-neutral nullvector with finite optimum forces the objective to annihilate ker Q and hence be constant on feasible closures. Corank one with known positive nullvector is a solved restricted case; higher nullity retains facet/circulation selection.

The projective account retains unbounded cross ratios at fixed oriented matroid and shows bounded-size coordinate jumps can incur coefficient-dependent progress. Exact collective solve/sign/ratio jumps escape an acquired narrow cone, but compatible slack acquisition is itself LP, and new tight rows need not be tight at the optimum. No general scaling, basis, circuit, strong oracle or permanent-progress operation is supplied for free. The reductions and counterexamples defeat these representations and rules; they do not establish a lower bound against all strongly polynomial algorithms.
